candidates.change_summary: Set the balance to msg.value instead of adding to the existing balance.
Add a fixed increment of 1 instead of msg.value to the caller's balance.
Delete the balance update statement so deposits are recorded nowhere.
Credit a hardcoded key instead of the caller, so a different mapping entry changes.
Return a constant 0 instead of the user's stored balance.
Return the balance incremented by one instead of the stored balance.
Replace the addition with multiplication so the recorded balance becomes balance * msg.value instead of balance + msg.value.
Delete the balance-update statement so deposits are never recorded.
Replace msg.value with the constant 1 so every call credits exactly 1 wei regardless of the amount sent.
Delete the statement that resets userBalance[msg.sender] to 0, so the caller's balance persists after withdrawal.
Move the zeroing of userBalance[msg.sender] to before the external call, so the balance is already zero when the call executes and stays zero on failure.
Delete the failure check `if (! _s) { revert(); }`, so the balance is zeroed even when the external call fails.
Delete the statement `userBalance[msg.sender] = 0;` so the caller's balance is not cleared after a successful withdrawal.
Move `userBalance[msg.sender] = 0;` to before the external call so the balance is already zero when the callee executes.
Delete `locked_ = false;` in the modifier so the contract stays locked after the first guarded call, making all subsequent withdrawBalance calls revert and leaving balances unchanged.
